fatal_errors: The reported 13.5% terminal strain is treated as a tensile uniform-elongation baseline, although it does not establish either tensile ductility or uniform elongation.

The supporting evidence concerns a stable single-phase FCC Co-Cr-Ni-V alloy; it does not validate cold rolling and recrystallization of the structurally and chemically distinct refractory Hf-Zr-Ti-Ta alloy.

No rolling reduction, annealing temperature, annealing time, or target phase state is specified, so the intervention is not reproducible and could instead cause cracking, phase evolution, oxidation, or excessive softening.
The proposed penetration test does not by itself separate chemical energy release from mechanical impact, fragmentation, and target heating.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the requested engineering objective and proposes matched tension, compression, and impact comparisons with a nominal falsification threshold, so it is a testable alternative in broad outline. It does not reconstruct the target intervention, which was systematic 1:1:1 Ta-Nb-V addition to HfZrTi, nor the associated HCP-to-BCC/omega phase evolution, solid-solution strengthening, adiabatic shear localization, and oxidation mechanism. Its conditions also omit defined quasi-static strain rates and the approximately 4000 s^-1 SHPB-in-air condition used to assess dynamic deformation and luminous energy release. The predicted increase beyond 20% uniform elongation is speculative and is based on incorrectly equating terminal strain with tensile uniform elongation. The cited FCC-alloy result provides only generic proof that recrystallized fine grains can yield a strength-ductility combination; it does not establish transferability to this refractory alloy or preservation of impact-triggered oxidation. The experiment would be more discriminating if processing parameters were fixed, tensile uniform and fracture elongations were distinguished, phase and texture changes were measured, and energy release were quantified under matched high-rate air and inert-atmosphere tests.
